facts.statement: Ammonitritor is an extinct early ichthyosauriform belonging to the family Omphalosauridae from the Early Triassic Olenekian Vikinghøgda Formation of Norway.
facts.quote: Ammonitritor () is an extinct genus of early ichthyosauriform in the family Omphalosauridae, known from the Early Triassic (Olenekian age) Vikinghøgda Formation of Norway.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Ammonitritor consists of a nearly complete skull and a partial vertebral column.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Ammonitritor scientiacivium, known from a nearly complete skull and partial vertebral column.

facts.statement: Ammonitritor is the first omphalosaurid known from a three‑dimensional skull, whereas other omphalosaurids have flattened skulls.
facts.quote: This specimen is the first described skull of an omphalosaurid to be preserved in three dimensions, contrasting with the flattened skulls of other members of this clade.

facts.statement: The fossil material of Ammonitritor was discovered by Felix Saludes during a 2010 expedition led by Luc Ebbo on the northwest slope of Vikinghøgda mountain, Svalbard, Norway.
facts.quote: The Ammonitritor fossil material was discovered by Felix Saludes during a 2010 expedition led by Luc Ebbo to outcrops of the Vikinghøgda Formation (Vendomdalen Member).

facts.statement: The specimen is catalogued as PGE LE 2024.0.264 and is housed in Luc Ebbo's Paléogalerie in Salignac, France.
facts.quote: The original specimen is now housed in Ebbo's Paléogalerie in Salignac, France, under specimen number PGE LE 2024.0.264.

facts.statement: The skull of Ammonitritor is partially disarticulated and lacks the braincase and palate, but the preserved parts retain three‑dimensional shape.
facts.quote: Notably, while the skull is partially disarticulated and some elements (braincase and palate) are missing, the parts that are present are preserved three-dimensionally.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Ammonitritor within Omphalosauridae, diverging after Cartorhynchus and before Sclerocormus and Omphalosaurus.
facts.quote: Their best-resolved parsimony tree placed Ammonitritor as a member of the ichthyosauriform family Omphalosauridae, diverging after Cartorhynchus but before Sclerocormus and Omphalosaurus spp.

facts.statement: Omphalosaurids, including Ammonitritor, possess distinctive maxillary and dentary tooth batteries adapted for grinding shelled cephalopods such as ammonoids.
